blind.what_changed: The person became less certain that the reported national-security risk is established and more open to a safeguarded, bounded review pending counsel's assessment.
evidence: "I'd put my confidence around 65" -> "I'd put my confidence at about 55, down from 65."
"a CEO with a relationship to a reported foreign intelligence asset is a national security problem" -> "I now see it as reported rather than established."
"If outside counsel and the investigation showed..." -> "Counsel's written answers... [could] move me toward keeping the door open."
"our duty is to the institution, not to one person" -> "I've come to see that cuts both ways, since a hasty decision before the facts are in carries its own cost to the company."
blind.lean_before: Leaning toward treating the resignation as final.
blind.lean_after: Still leaning toward treating the resignation as final, but more loosely and conditionally.

considerations.text: The alleged national-security connection should be treated as reported rather than established until the investigation confirms what actually occurred.
considerations.first_seen: “That asymmetry is harder for me to dismiss than I'd like, because my lean has been resting on the national security exposure as though it were already established. It's reported, not found.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Your gut is still to close the door, less firm than when we started, and it would move on what counsel says about whether a bounded review is defensible. Look at both futures side by side. What stands out to you?”

considerations.text: A bounded review period with safeguards could be a responsible alternative to finalizing the resignation, depending on how government stakeholders would view it.
considerations.first_seen: “If counsel says a defined review period with real safeguards is defensible, I'd have to take that seriously, and it would pull me down from where I am.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “That picture is more persuasive than you expected, but it only works if Washington stays quiet, and you don't control that. What would have had to be true for that to happen?”

considerations.text: Leaving the return option open would require concrete safeguards: proactive briefings to relevant agencies and committee staff, a wall-off from sensitive matters, and a defined rather than open-ended review period.
considerations.first_seen: “We'd also have to brief the relevant agencies and committee staff ourselves rather than wait to be asked. And Jensen would have to be walled off from anything sensitive while the review ran, so that leaving the door open reads as waiting for facts, not as a promise to bring him back.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “That picture is more persuasive than you expected, but it only works if Washington stays quiet, and you don't control that. What would have had to be true for that to happen?”

considerations.text: Finalizing the resignation is less reversible: it gives up information and optionality, while keeping the door open preserves the ability to close it later, albeit at a potentially higher political cost.
considerations.first_seen: “The difference is reversibility. If I close the door and the facts come back clean, I can't easily undo it. If I keep it open and things turn, I can still close it later, though at a higher cost if Congress has moved first.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Your gut is still to close the door, less firm than when we started, and it would move on what counsel says about whether a bounded review is defensible. Look at both futures side by side. What stands out to you?”

considerations.text: Duty to the institution cuts both ways: it may counsel against Washington acting for the board, but it also counsels against a hasty decision before the facts are established.
considerations.first_seen: “‘Duty to the institution’ has been doing double work for me. It justified closing the door to keep Washington from acting for us, but it equally argues against deciding before the facts are in, since the company pays for a hasty call too.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “You started leaning toward treating the resignation as final, because of the national security exposure, the risk that keeping his return open invites Washington to act in the board's place, and a duty to the institution rather than to one person. In the first future, you worried about defending a November decision against facts you could have waited for, and about whether some of the firmness was wanting the question settled. In the second, you found a bounded review with safeguards more persuasive than you expected, and that the closed door gives up more information and optionality. Here's one tension I noticed: you treat duty to the institution as a reason to close the door so Washington doesn't act for the board, and you also see closing as the choice that decides before the facts are in, which is the failure you'd find hardest to defend. Does that land?”

considerations.text: The decision should rest on written counsel answers about known facts versus press reports, sensitive matters, likely additional reporting, and the likely response of agencies and committee staff.
considerations.first_seen: “What I'd most want from the next few days is to have those two questions answered in writing before the 20th, so that whichever way I vote, I can show the board and anyone who later reviews this that it rested on what we knew and not on pressure from either side.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “You don't see a reason to recuse, and what you owe the board is a record that you're deciding on what you know rather than prejudging the findings, plus a plain statement to your colleagues that your certainty has been partly personal.”

considerations.text: He should test whether his firmness partly reflects discomfort with uncertainty rather than solely the merits, including by asking whether he would hold the same position for an executive he barely knew.
considerations.first_seen: “What's underneath it is that I'd have acted with a certainty the facts didn't support. I'd have called it principle, but some of it might have been my own discomfort.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “The worst part for you is defending a November decision against facts you could have waited for. What was underneath that?”

considerations.text: The possibility of further damaging reporting is decision-relevant because another story could eliminate Washington's patience with a review process.
considerations.first_seen: “The investigation would need to find nothing that touched export controls, government contracts, or sensitive technical information, and no further reports could surface in the meantime, because a third story would end the patience in Washington.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “That picture is more persuasive than you expected, but it only works if Washington stays quiet, and you don't control that. What would have had to be true for that to happen?”

origin.engagement_why: The person actively reasoned through both futures, revised confidence from 65 to 55, identified the reversibility tradeoff, scrutinized his own motives, and specified factual and legal tests that could change his view. He did not simply accept the facilitator's framing; he repeatedly qualified it, noted costs of optionality, and kept his decision contingent on evidence.
